about: Denning's rulings on findings and detections, used to calibrate rules.py. One entry per ruling.

labels.ruling: agree: missed (131 s); on time is about 15 s, 60 s is definitely late

labels.rule: lone ranger: Mes/A plus frontline collapse
labels.ruling: 8 monk defending was likely wrong, but a real trade-off (keeps all damage at main); needs data
losing the stand that close is normal; it shows the capping team was down on flags
one damage pushing is likely fine, depending on the pusher and the runner; whether always collapsing is better needs data
not a split: a full team collapse

labels.rule: 8 monk in base after the pit died
labels.ruling: right call: a Mes/A can't hold a ranger once the pit is dead

great play by hdm, not a failure by HC: even 8v8, monks in position, 8 tried to Guardian the prot but was interrupted, prot stripped, 7 and prot knocked down, 8 Dazed; acceptable mistakes: 8 casting beside the ranger without faking, prot not keeping Aura of Stability on the 7, mesmers not interrupting defensively; interrupts on Reversal of Fortune and Aegis were luck; pre-kiting with a stance was correct; hitting the Mes/A was correct peel

casting beside the ranger is a minor mistake (high level, not always avoidable), not acceptable; with the 8 alone it could be game ending after time. The 8's 3-man group was correct. The mesmer should always interrupt defensively there, and someone should have peeled so the 8 could kite; the 8 should probably have cancel-cast. Open: was Men on its way to cap or pinned, could the 8 kite into its pit

Men was running a flag, so HC had to run too to avoid falling behind (cap as soon as reasonably possible after the enemy); HC couldn't retreat to its pit. The cause was probably the Daze (a slight misplay), but the bigger issue was the flag and where HC's fifth damage (the Mes/A) was
